name: Jiongnai Bunu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Mao Zongwu & Li Yunbing 2002, Jiongnaiyu yanjiu [A Study of Jiongnai] (Central Univ. for Nationalities Press); not online

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kiong Nai language' (en) and '炯奈语' (zh), read 2026-09-17
sources.note: zh page gives Longhua/Changdong phonology from Mao & Li 2002 and Chen 2013 (7 vowels, 8 tones 44 33 53 31 35 11 55 12, tones 7-8 with -ʔ); neither page says anything about stress or 轻声.

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien language history. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: ANU. hdl:1885/146760
sources.note: 29 mentions of Jiongnai (Longhua data via Wang & Mao 1995) but no Jiongnai-specific stress remark; only family-level notes: p.28 Mien iambic rhythm quoting Downer 1961 ('weaker stress and shorter duration than the following full syllables'), p.199 Hmong-Mien nominal prefixes 'are unstressed'.

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2003. Review of Mao Zongwu and Li Yunbing, Jiongnaiyu Yanjiu [A study of Jiongnai]. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 26(1): 119-121. doi:10.32655/ltba.26.1.06
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States the reviewed grammar's layout: phonology pp. 1-19, word-formation/Chinese loans pp. 20-39, syntax pp. 40-83, Longhua-vs-Liuxiang dialect comparison pp. 84-93, Hmong-Mien comparison pp. 94-253, glossary and a text.

sources.citation: 田口善久 [Taguchi, Yoshihisa]. 1996. 炯奈話調査報告 [A study on Jiong Nai dialect]. 言語文化論叢 (Papers on languages and cultures, Chiba University) 2: 17-24.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1 (音韻と音声) on the Liuxiang village variety covers tones (Longhua 44 33 53 31 35 11 55 12 after Chen 1991; Liuxiang 44 42 35 54 33 31 43/55 21), prenasalized initials, nasal and stop codas; sec. 2 numerals. No word on stress or accent anywhere in the 8 pages (scanned PDF read from page renders; only eng tesseract available, no jpn scanned).

sources.citation: Chen Qiguang 陈其光. 2013. 苗瑶语文 [Miao-Yao languages]. Beijing: 中央民族大学出版社 (Jiongnai pp. 362-368).
